title: Default insight list order must use an indexed column (-last_modified_at, -pk), not the vestigial Insight.order
answers: Why is the insights API slow when no order param is passed?
Insight list endpoint takes tens of seconds per page / pins web workers
What is the default sort order of /api/projects/:id/insights/?
Is it safe to sort insights by the `order` field?
body:
Symptom: API clients listing insights without an `order` query param wait tens of seconds per page; every offset page repeats the cost, and the load hits the shared Postgres primary.
Root cause: products/product_analytics/backend/presentation/insight.py:InsightViewSet.order_queryset fell back to `order_by("order")`. `Insight.order` is a vestigial nullable integer with no index (NULL on almost every row), so Postgres scanned and sorted the whole project, and pagination was non-deterministic (all rows in one NULL group).
Fix pattern: default to `order_by("-last_modified_at", "-pk")`. The partial index `dashboarditem_team_lmod_idx` on `(team_id, -last_modified_at) WHERE NOT deleted` covers it, so the sort can seek and the LIMIT stops early. This also stops the correlated `with_last_viewed_at` subquery from running for every row. `-pk` breaks ties so pages stay stable.
Constraints: any new default or ordering branch in order_queryset should match an existing index and include a pk tie-breaker. Do not add an index on `order`; that option was rejected because the column is vestigial. The `search` branch still returns the queryset unsorted so relevance ranking applies. The app's own list views send `order=-last_modified_at` explicitly. Changing the default changes the response order for external API clients, so treat it as a customer-visible change.
applies: Insight list API ordering in InsightViewSet.order_queryset (product_analytics backend)
